answer: An admission auction stops identity forgery by selling entry slots to the top sealed bidders. Only 100 slots open per epoch, so 1,000 fakes need ten epochs of wins, and each bid joins a gale that lifts the clearing price: the thousandth fake costs far more than the first. Winning bids stay locked like a glacier and thaw after verified work, so the same funds cannot fund the next batch; 1,000 fakes cost over 200,000 credits. A bid-ring pays the inflated price, since sealed bids hide rivals. An honest agent buys one slot once and keeps its full share until the epoch horizon.
